CRM notes: workshop-heavy account — focused on dedicated capacity for transaction processing + live agent chat. Key fragments below.

Summary of needs:
- Workload: mix of agent chat (customer support), real-time transaction reranking (fraud/risk scoring), and nightly embeddings for search indexing.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 220ms for chat agent messages (avg request 3-4 turns), p99 goal 400ms; reranking p95 <= 120ms for top-k scoring path.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state QPS target: 250 QPS (business hours), average tokens per request (inc response) ~80-100 tokens -> ~20k tokens/sec baseline.
- Peaks: traffic spikes during batch payment windows and sales events — modelling shows bursts up to 1,200 QPS for 3-10 minute windows (estimate ~96k tokens/sec at peak). Need autoscale/burst capacity without impacting SLA.
- Desired throughput guarantee: reserved capacity to comfortably sustain 250 QPS @ p95 SLA; soft guarantee for 600-800 QPS with autoscale; explicit peak plan to cover 1,200 QPS with burst capacity and price-on-use.

Workshop outcomes / recommended sizing (SE draft):
- Initial reserved commit: 8 x H100-style GPUs (on-prem-style perf model) sized to meet baseline and provide headroom for steady growth.
- Autoscale burst policy: instant scale up to 16 GPUs for scheduled events; optional hot standby fleet of 4 smaller GPUs for fast fallbacks.
- Model split: primary inference on a quantized 70B variant for ranking/complex chat; low-latency fallback routes to a 13B quantized model for sub-200ms p95 on small prompts.
- Caching: prefix + KV cache for repeat transaction patterns; embedding cache for similar merchant vectors. Expected to reduce token/sec by ~18% in steady-state.
- Batching profile: adaptive batching with latency SLO target 95th percentile gating; conservative batch sizes during interactive chat, aggressive batching for reranking offline jobs.

SLA / commercial points discussed:
- P95 latency SLA target requested by Solaris: 220ms for chat on reserved capacity; Redwood to propose measurable SLO + credit schedule.
- Uptime: enterprise 99.9% SLA requested; Redwood to provide incident playbook and on-call contact.
- Pricing: three-tier approach presented — reserved monthly commit (8 GPUs), burst hours billed at a premium, and usage credits for autoscale events.
- Term: Solaris prefers 12-18 month committed capacity with quarterly review.

- Data residency: primary region US-East, secondary EU for cross-border customer support.
